findings.message: The fix covers only one direction. The link note now follows the edited work email through `tool.note` → `checkCardEdits` → FormConfirm `info`. But the card title still says ` · links to X's sign-in`, and that title is built once, from the email the card was created with. Nothing rebuilds it when the email is edited. If the person changes the email away from a linkable account, the note goes away but the title still promises the link. The card then contradicts itself, and the header claims a link that addPerson won't make. Fix: take the link out of the static title and show it only through `linkNote`. Show that note on the first render too, by working it out once from the starting input, so one source decides it.
findings.scenario: Ask chat to "add Priya Jayasena to HR" with workEmail priya@lumenlabs.test. The card title reads 'Add Priya Jayasena to HR · links to Priya Jayasena's sign-in'. Edit Work email to priya.j@example.test. The check returns no note, but the title still says it links to Priya's sign-in. Confirm, and the record is created with user_id null.

findings.message: The new race test doesn't prove the lock. (1) It doesn't run the real job. It acts out `extendStanding` by hand, with a hand-written `select … for update` and a planted insert, so a change to how the job locks or fills is never tested. (2) It orders the two sessions with a fixed 400 ms sleep. If `set(...)` hasn't reached its delete before the holding transaction commits, the delete sees the committed 2028-01 row and removes it whether or not `lockStanding` exists, so the test can pass with the lock deleted. (3) Only the end path is tested. The other two writers that round 2 changed to lock first have no race test: the hand-set path and the hand-removal path (`setAllocation` with `percent: 0` → `skipMonths`, services.ts:60–67). Fix: run `extendStanding` itself in session A. Pause it after its lock with a test hook or an advisory lock, and wait until session B is actually blocked (poll `pg_locks`/`pg_stat_activity` for a lock wait) rather than sleeping. Run the test for all three writers: end, hand set, and hand removal. Check that each case fails when `lockStanding` is removed.
findings.scenario: Delete the `lockStanding` call in setStanding and run the test on a slow CI runner where `set()` takes more than 400 ms to resolve the person and project. The delete runs after the holding transaction commits, so 2028-01 is removed and the test still passes.

findings.message: The refusal text 'matches more than one person; use the employee number' is still written twice: here and in services.ts:30 `personOf`. The resolver is now shared, but the two messages can drift apart. Fix: build the message in `resolvePerson`'s module, or return it with the `ambiguous` result, and use it in both places.
